name: Isolated Encephalocele

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Encephalocele

criteria.description: Presence of a congenital skull defect with herniation of intracranial contents
Neuroimaging (MRI or CT) demonstrating herniation of brain tissue and/or meninges through the skull defect
No associated major congenital malformations or syndromic features (isolated presentation)
Visible cranial swelling or sac-like protrusion at birth or detected prenatally

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a congenital skull defect with herniation of intracranial contents confirmed by neuroimaging, without other major malformations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological; genetic testing may be considered to exclude syndromic causes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital cranial bone defect with herniation of brain tissue
searchTerms: skull bone defect with brain bulge
congenital skull opening with brain tissue protrusion
birth defect causing brain tissue herniation through skull

pathognomonic.symptomName: Visible sac-like protrusion on the scalp or skull

common.notes: May develop secondary to CSF flow obstruction
Variable severity depending on brain involvement
May occur due to cortical dysplasia or brain injury

occasional.notes: Due to involvement of occipital lobe or optic pathways
Hemiparesis or spasticity depending on lesion location

rare.notes: Secondary to brainstem involvement or aspiration

searchTerms: increased brain pressure from fluid buildup

rare.notes: Rarely observed depending on lesion location
searchTerms: cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

laboratory: CSF analysis if hydrocephalus or infection suspected
imaging: MRI showing herniation of brain tissue and meninges through skull defect
CT scan demonstrating bony defect and associated brain abnormalities
Ultrasound prenatal screening may detect encephalocele
genetic: No specific isolated encephalocele gene identified
Genetic testing to exclude syndromic causes such as Meckel-Gruber syndrome
other: Physical examination revealing cranial swelling or sac
Neurological assessment for developmental and motor deficits

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of multiple congenital anomalies including renal cystic dysplasia
Herniation of meninges only without brain tissue

redFlags: Rapid increase in size of encephalocele sac
Signs of increased intracranial pressure (vomiting, irritability)
references: Barkovich AJ. Pediatric Neuroimaging. 5th ed. Lippincott Williams & Wilkins; 2012.
Moore KL, Persaud TVN. The Developing Human: Clinically Oriented Embryology. 10th ed. Elsevier; 2015.
